headline: High: Flowise’s writable, broad-egress orchestration can amplify Argo outputs into unsafe downstream actions and data exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo can emit API/GRPC-driven workflow outputs, and Flowise runs graph-based tool flows with browser and filesystem access. A shared handoff path is plausible, but no direct shared channel is documented, so I rate this as medium rather than high. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, not observed.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are copied into a Flowise node or file input without sanitization
IF Flowise treats imported text or files as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and schema for Argo outputs before Flowise ingests them
Disable any Flowise node that auto-parses free-form text as instructions
Use a read-only handoff file with explicit provenance labels
Review one sample workflow for prompt-injection markers before enabling it
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware filtering between the systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while Flowise reads and writes server filesystem files and sends data to model providers and configured HTTP/search tools. That creates a plausible shared-data path with sensitive artifacts flowing into a broader-egress agent. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so I keep this at medium, not high.
conditions: IF Argo artifacts or parameters are placed in a Flowise-accessible directory
IF Flowise flows forward those files or inputs to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Restrict Flowise to a dedicated non-sensitive workspace
Remove secrets from Argo artifacts before handoff
Turn off file-upload nodes in Flowise for this pairing
Check one workflow for outbound calls to third-party providers
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists at the orchestrator boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo has allowlisted network egress and API/GRPC surfaces, while Flowise has broad egress plus writable filesystem access and shared state via server datastore. Even without explicit git or shell write overlap, both can mutate shared external resources if pointed at the same backend, so conflict is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or datastore
IF Flowise flows call back into Argo-managed resources without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories for each agent
Use per-agent credentials for any shared backend
Disable concurrent writes to the same datastore
Run a quick lock test on one shared resource
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency or locking around shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo can produce workflow artifacts and parameters that Flowise may consume as tool-flow inputs. Flowise’s graph-based orchestration and external tool/model calls mean it can act on those inputs without a built-in verification step in the profile, so a bad Argo output can cascade into irreversible downstream actions or exfiltration.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Argo-produced artifacts as authoritative inputs
IF a Flowise node triggers external tools, emails, or API actions from those inputs
mitigations: Insert a human review step between Argo and Flowise
Require Flowise to validate Argo outputs against a schema
Disable action-taking nodes until validation passes
Log one end-to-end run and inspect for unchecked propagation
requires-engineering: add signed outputs from Argo and signature checks in Flowise

E_compliance.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets such as model provider keys and tool credentials. The profiles show different data classes and retention-sensitive surfaces, but no explicit residency or certification mismatch, so this is a medium compliance risk rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Flowise chatflow inputs or outputs
IF Argo artifacts contain data subject to stricter retention than Flowise storage
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it through either system
Keep regulated data out of Flowise chatflows
Review retention settings for both systems
Export one sample record and verify deletion behavior
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
